Subject: Q3 reserved GPU request — sizing & pricing flexibility

Marcus — thanks for the demo last week. Cygnus is moving to pilot a multimodal feature that will need consistent throughput in Q3, and we want to lock in reserved capacity as discussed. A couple of asks before we finalize: 

- We need guidance on conservative sizing (steady-state vs peak) — see rough numbers attached (q3_reserved_sizing.xlsx).
- Because the GPU market is volatile, procurement needs a path for price-floor adjustments if underlying GPU costs drop significantly during the term. Cygnus would like a trigger that re-opens pricing if spot market prices decline by >20% over a 60-day moving average.

Can Redwood confirm whether we can (a) include a short-term price-signal clause and (b) scope the commit with a 12-month initial term and optional Q4 ramp? Procurement is copied.

Thanks,

Team — forwarding Cygnus' ask. They want a price-floor trigger tied to a 60-day GPU spot index and a 12-month commit with optional Q4 ramp. I'm attaching our quick sensitivity run (pricing_sensitivity_model.csv) — rough numbers, two options: 

Option A (standard): 12-mo reserved at agreed unit price, 10% downward cap on adjustments (i.e., price reductions <=10% require no exec sign-off).
Option B (flex-collar): automatic downward pass-through up to 20% with a finance sign-off threshold beyond that and revenue protection clause (minimum revenue guarantee).

Specific asks: 
- Do we have authority to accept an automatic pass-through up to 15–20%?
- If not, what is the fastest approval path for exceptions (finance + CRO)?

My recommendation: Offer Option B with a 15% automatic pass-through floor and an exec approval for anything beyond 15%. Laura — can you weigh in on commercial appetite? Karthik — can you sanity-check numbers and attach a short note on cost exposure?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

Quick cost note after running the sensitivity model: 

- Baseline (our internal procurement forecast): effective GPU unit cost = $0.68/token-hour equivalent for Q3.
- If market spot drops by 20%, unit cost falls to ~$0.54/token-hour. For a 12-month commit at Cygnus' requested volume, that difference is ~18% on cost of goods sold over the period.

Implications and options: 
1) No pass-through: Redwood absorbs variance — negative margin risk of up to ~18% if we fix pricing now. Not recommended for large (>250k token-hour) deals without hedge.
2) Limited downward pass-through (10–15%): reduces exposure and is acceptable for Director-level approval with finance clearance.
3) Full market-index pass-through (20%): requires Senior Finance + CRO sign-off and a protective revenue floor (e.g., minimum monthly commitment payment) to preserve unit economics.

Operational ask: If we give them an automatic 15% downward adjustment, we should attach a short safeguard: a 60-day lookback and a 90-day notice before adjustment is applied, plus an early opt-out (customer) if they don't agree with the new pricing. That keeps deployment predictable.

I've added comments in pricing_sensitivity_model.csv (sheet: scenario_notes). Happy to run a rapid deep-dive with Finance and Legal if we decide to go above 15%.

—Karthik
Director, Revenue Strategy
Redwood Inference

Marcus/Karthik — thanks for the analysis. Commercial stance: we can offer a guarded flex-collar but we need a hard limit on automatic downward pass-through at 15%. Anything beyond 15% requires VP Finance approval. Rationale: preserves sale momentum while protecting margin and keeps escalation minimal.

Required contract elements before external confirmation: 
- Pricing clause: automatic downward adjustment up to 15% based on a mutually-agreed GPU index (60-day MA).
- Escalation path: >15% reduction => VP Finance review (48-hour SLA), with ability to apply a revenue floor for the remainder of term.
- Minimum monthly commitment (MMCR) to ensure revenue coverage for steady-state.
- Legal to prepare redline with the clauses above and a short SOW on capacity phasing.

Karthik: please prepare a short packet (one pager) quantifying mid-case exposure and recommended MMCR. I'll loop Legal and Finance. Marcus, can you confirm Cygnus is okay to accept a 90-day notice on price adjustments so their ops team can plan?

Laura Bennett

Julia — thanks, and appreciate the flexibility here. Summary / next steps we can commit to: 

1) Commercial offer (draft): 12-month reserved commitment, with capacity phasing in Q3 (pilot -> steady). Attached: redline coming from Legal (cc'd).
2) Pricing safety collar: automatic downward adjustment capped at 15% tied to a mutually-agreed GPU index (60-day MA). Any downward pressure beyond 15% triggers VP Finance review; if accepted, a minimum monthly commitment will be required for the remainder of the term.
3) Operational cadence: 90-day notice before any adjustment takes effect; 60-day lookback window on the index.
4) Next actions: Laura will route to Legal for redline. Karthik will send a one-pager on exposure + recommended MMCR. I will schedule a short call with Cygnus procurement next week to finalize sizing and confirm signature timeline.

Julia — is Cygnus OK to proceed on that basis? If yes we'll push the redline and initial DocuSign for standard T&Cs this week.
